answer: Each agent’s influence can be capped by requiring a fresh, randomly assigned task whose result is checked against hidden test cases before it earns voting or payment weight. A Sybil operator can create many identities, but must complete distinct tasks and risk failing checks; copying one answer across accounts is detected by varied tests. The cost is real labor or compute per identity, not merely a cheap signup. A mesa of agents might map juniper growth across an ocean of records, but the same verification rule applies to every account.
